claim: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) belongs to male infertility due to spermatogenesis failure.
source: Non-obstructive azoospermia (NOA) belongs to male infertility due to spermatogenesis failure.
evidence: This is a definitional statement presented in the abstract that establishes the nature of NOA.

claim: HE staining confirmed the structural abnormalities of the seminiferous tubules in NOA patients.
source: HE staining confirmed the structural abnormalities of the seminiferous tubules in NOA patients.
evidence: The manuscript reports experimental results from HE staining showing structural abnormalities.

claim: 12 germ cell subtypes were identified: spermatogonial stem cell-0 (SSC0), SSC1, SSC2, diffing-spermatogonia (Diffing-SPG), diffed-spermatogonia (Diffed-SPG), pre-leptotene (Pre-Lep), leptotene-zygotene (L-Z), pachytene (Pa), diplotene (Di), spermatids-1 (SPT1), SPT2, and SPT3.
source: We identified 12 germ cell subtypes (spermatogonial stem cell-0 [SSC0], SSC1, SSC2, diffing-spermatogonia [Diffing-SPG], diffed-spermatogonia [Diffed-SPG], pre-leptotene [Pre-Lep], leptotene-zygotene [L-Z], pachytene [Pa], diplotene [Di], spermatids-1 [SPT1], SPT2, and SPT3)
evidence: This is a direct result from the scRNA-seq analysis performed in the study.

claim: 8 Sertoli cell subtypes were identified (SC1-SC8).
source: We identified 12 germ cell subtypes (spermatogonial stem cell-0 [SSC0], SSC1, SSC2, diffing-spermatogonia [Diffing-SPG], diffed-spermatogonia [Diffed-SPG], pre-leptotene [Pre-Lep], leptotene-zygotene [L-Z], pachytene [Pa], diplotene [Di], spermatids-1 [SPT1], SPT2, and SPT3) and 8 Sertoli cell subtypes (SC1-SC8).
evidence: This is a direct result from the scRNA-seq analysis performed in the study.

claim: Three novel Sertoli cell subtype phenotypes were identified: SC4/immature, SC7/mature, and SC8/further mature Sertoli cells.
source: Among them, three novel Sertoli cell subtype phenotypes were identified, namely SC4/immature, SC7/mature, and SC8/further mature Sertoli cells.
evidence: This is a novel finding reported from the analysis of Sertoli cell subtypes.

claim: ST3GAL4, A2M, ASB9, and TEX19 co-localize with DDX4 (classical marker of germ cell) as confirmed by immunofluorescence.
source: For each germ or Sertoli cell subtype, we identified unique new markers, among which immunofluorescence confirmed co-localization of ST3GAL4, A2M, ASB9, and TEX19 and DDX4 (classical marker of germ cell).
evidence: This is an experimental validation using immunofluorescence to confirm marker co-localization.

claim: PRAP1, BST2, and CCDC62 were co-expressed with SOX9 (classical marker of Sertoli cell) in testes tissues as confirmed by immunofluorescence.
source: PRAP1, BST2, and CCDC62 were co-expressed with SOX9 (classical marker of Sertoli cell) in testes tissues also confirmed by immunofluorescence.
evidence: This is an experimental validation using immunofluorescence to confirm marker co-expression.

claim: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern.
source: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern, as evidenced by SC1/2/5/7 involving in SSC0-2 development, SC3 participating in the whole process of spermiogenesis, SC4/6 participating in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development, and SC8 involving in the final stage of SPT3.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of cell-cell interactions in the study.

claim: SC1/2/5/7 are involved in SSC0-2 development.
source: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern, as evidenced by SC1/2/5/7 involving in SSC0-2 development, SC3 participating in the whole process of spermiogenesis, SC4/6 participating in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development, and SC8 involving in the final stage of SPT3.
evidence: This is a specific finding about stage-specific interactions between cell subtypes.

claim: SC3 participates in the whole process of spermiogenesis.
source: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern, as evidenced by SC1/2/5/7 involving in SSC0-2 development, SC3 participating in the whole process of spermiogenesis, SC4/6 participating in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development, and SC8 involving in the final stage of SPT3.
evidence: This is a specific finding about stage-specific interactions between cell subtypes.

claim: SC4/6 participate in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development.
source: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern, as evidenced by SC1/2/5/7 involving in SSC0-2 development, SC3 participating in the whole process of spermiogenesis, SC4/6 participating in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development, and SC8 involving in the final stage of SPT3.
evidence: This is a specific finding about stage-specific interactions between cell subtypes.

claim: SC8 is involved in the final stage of SPT3.
source: The interaction between germ cell subtypes and Sertoli cell subtypes exhibits stage-specific-matching pattern, as evidenced by SC1/2/5/7 involving in SSC0-2 development, SC3 participating in the whole process of spermiogenesis, SC4/6 participating in Diffing and Diffed-SPG development, and SC8 involving in the final stage of SPT3.
evidence: This is a specific finding about stage-specific interactions between cell subtypes.

claim: The interaction between germ cells and Sertoli cells is mainly regulated by the Notch1/2/3 signaling.
source: The interaction was mainly regulated by the Notch1/2/3 signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cell communication analysis performed in the study.

claim: Infertility affects approximately 15% of couples.
source: Infertility is a common disease affecting approximately 15% of couples, and 50% of cases in infertility is attributed to male factor infertility (Agarwal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from the literature (Agarwal et al., 2015).

claim: 50% of infertility cases are attributed to male factor infertility.
source: Infertility is a common disease affecting approximately 15% of couples, and 50% of cases in infertility is attributed to male factor infertility (Agarwal et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from the literature (Agarwal et al., 2015).

claim: Male infertility is mainly associated with sexual dysfunction, endocrine, varicocele, and reproductive system infection.
source: Male infertility is mainly associated with sexual dysfunction, endocrine, varicocele, and reproductive system infection (Naz and Kamal, 2017).
evidence: This is a cited statement from the literature (Naz and Kamal, 2017).

claim: NOA accounts for about 1% of adult males and 10–15% of infertile males.
source: NOA accounts for about 1% of adult males and 10–15% of infertile males (Fakhro et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited statistic from the literature (Fakhro et al., 2018).

claim: The etiology of NOA includes cryptorchidism, post-pubertal mumps orchitis, and prior testicular torsion.
source: The etiology of NOA is varied, including cryptorchidism, post-pubertal mumps orchitis, and prior testicular torsion (Yao et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a cited statement from the literature (Yao et al., 2022).

claim: The formation of mature spermatozoa can be delineated into three stages: the proliferation of spermatogonial cells, meiotic division of spermatocytes, and the maturation of sperm cells.
source: The formation of mature spermatozoa can be delineated into three stages: the proliferation of spermatogonial cells, meiotic division of spermatocytes, and the maturation of sperm cells (Jégou, 1993).
evidence: This is a cited statement from the literature (Jégou, 1993) describing the stages of spermatogenesis.

claim: The seminiferous tubule comprises three distinct cell types: Sertoli cells, germ cells of various generations, and peritubular cells.
source: The seminiferous tubule comprises three distinct cell types: Sertoli cells, extending from the basal membrane to the tubular lumen; germ cells of various generations; and peritubular cells, surrounding Sertoli cells and germ cells, isolated from Sertoli cells by the extracellular matrix.
evidence: This is a description of the cellular composition of seminiferous tubules based on established knowledge.

claim: In most mammals, germ cells undergo continuous renewal, while Sertoli cells cease division during the pubertal developmental period.
source: In most mammals, germ cells undergo continuous renewal, while Sertoli cells cease division during the pubertal developmental period, forming the seminiferous epithelium.
evidence: This is a statement about the developmental biology of mammalian reproductive cells based on established knowledge.

claim: Adult spermatogonial stem cells are distributed along the basal membrane at the base of the seminiferous tubule.
source: Adult spermatogonial stem cells are distributed along the basal membrane at the base of the seminiferous tubule, necessitating a delicate balance between self-renewal and differentiation.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomical location of spermatogonial stem cells based on established knowledge.

claim: Only Sertoli cells consistently maintain physical contact with sperm cells throughout spermatogenesis.
source: Throughout this process, only Sertoli cells consistently maintain physical contact with sperm cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the unique relationship between Sertoli cells and germ cells based on established knowledge.

claim: The entire process of spermatogenesis inevitably involves intense information exchange with Sertoli cells.
source: Consequently, we posit that the entire process of spermatogenesis inevitably involves intense information exchange with the occurrence of Sertoli cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on the known relationship between Sertoli cells and germ cells.

claim: scRNA-seq technology is used for high-throughput molecular detection of a single cell and exploring the whole-gene expression profiles of a single cell.
source: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology is used for high-throughput molecular detection of a single cell and exploring the whole-gene expression profiles of a single cell (Tan et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a cited description of scRNA-seq technology from the literature (Tan et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2020).

claim: scRNA-seq can delineate the existence of rare cell subsets and the degree of cellular heterogeneity.
source: It can delineate the existence of rare cell subsets and the degree of cellular heterogeneity (Tirumalasetty et al., 2024; Vértesy et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a cited capability of scRNA-seq technology from the literature (Tirumalasetty et al., 2024; Vértesy et al., 2018).

claim: Liao et al., 2019 performed scRNA-seq analysis on mouse testicular germ cells at 5.5 days after birth, revealing the heterogeneity of gene expression in undifferentiated spermatogonial cells.
source: Liao et al., 2019 performed scRNA-seq analysis on mouse testicular germ cells at 5.5 days after birth, revealing the heterogeneity of gene expression in undifferentiated spermatogonial cells.
evidence: This is a cited study from the literature (Liao et al., 2019).

claim: Guo et al., 2018 performed scRNA-seq of testicular cells from young adults and found that there were five different spermatogonial states accompanying human spermatogonial differentiation.
source: Guo et al., 2018 performed scRNA-seq of testicular cells from young adults and found that there were five different spermatogonial states accompanying human spermatogonial differentiation.
evidence: This is a cited study from the literature (Guo et al., 2018).

claim: scATAC-seq is a widely used method to obtain a genome-wide snapshot of chromatin accessibility, signatures of active transcription and transcription factor (TF) binding.
source: In addition, single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) is a widely used method to obtain a genome-wide snapshot of chromatin accessibility, signatures of active transcription and transcription factor (TF) binding (Mimitou et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a cited description of scATAC-seq technology from the literature (Mimitou et al., 2021).

claim: Cellular identity is strongly affected by the epigenetic wiring of the cell, which is measured by scATAC-seq.
source: Cellular identity is strongly affected by the epigenetic wiring of the cell, which is measured by scATAC-seq (Pervolarakis et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a cited statement from the literature (Pervolarakis et al., 2020) about the utility of scATAC-seq.

claim: In the OA1-P1 group, seminiferous tubules displayed normal structure with well-organized layers of germ cells at various stages of spermatogenesis, including mature spermatozoa.
source: In the OA1-P1 group, seminiferous tubules displayed normal structure with well-organized layers of germ cells at various stages of spermatogenesis, including mature spermatozoa.
evidence: This is a description of histological observations from HE staining shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the OA2-P2 group, germ cells and spermatozoa were present but show disorganized arrangement, with sloughed cells observed in the lumen.
source: In the OA2-P2 group, germ cells and spermatozoa were present but show disorganized arrangement, with sloughed cells observed in the lumen.
evidence: This is a description of histological observations from HE staining shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the NOA1-P3 group, no spermatozoa were present, but a small number of spermatocytes and spermatogonia were visible, along with various stages of spermatogenesis.
source: In the NOA1-P3 group, no spermatozoa were present, but a small number of spermatocytes and spermatogonia were visible, along with various stages of spermatogenesis.
evidence: This is a description of histological observations from HE staining shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the NOA2-P4 group, germ cells and spermatozoa were present but exhibit disordered arrangement, with sloughed cells in the lumen.
source: In the NOA2-P4 group, germ cells and spermatozoa were present but exhibit disordered arrangement, with sloughed cells in the lumen.
evidence: This is a description of histological observations from HE staining shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the NOA3-P5 group, only Sertoli cells were observed, indicating impaired spermatogenesis.
source: In the NOA3-P5 group, only Sertoli cells were observed, indicating impaired spermatogenesis (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of histological observations from HE staining shown in Figure 1A, with an interpretation of impaired spermatogenesis.

claim: After removing low-quality cells, 23,889 cells were obtained for scRNA-seq.
source: After removing low-quality cells, we obtained 23,889 cells for scRNA-seq (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the scRNA-seq data processing.

claim: The quantity of annotated germ cells in patients categorized as NOA1, NOA2, and NOA3 gradually decreased to zero.
source: Notably, the quantity of annotated germ cells in patients categorized as NOA1, NOA2, and NOA3 gradually decreased to zero (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the scRNA-seq data analysis.

claim: UMAP analysis of scRNA-seq revealed 12 major cell types, including germ cells, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, endothelial cells, peritubular myoid cells (PMCs), smooth muscle, Schwann cell, macrophage, mast cells, T cells, B cells, and plasma cells.
source: UMAP analysis of scRNA-seq revealed 12 major cell types, including germ cells, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, endothelial cells, peritubular myoid cells (PMCs), smooth muscle, Schwann cell, macrophage, mast cells, T cells, B cells, and plasma cells (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a result from the UMAP analysis of scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A total of 41,708 high-quality cells were obtained from scATAC-seq analysis.
source: A total of 41,708 high-quality cells were obtained from scATAC-seq analysis (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the scATAC-seq data processing.

claim: scATAC-seq identified B cells, endothelial cells, PMCs, Schwann cell, smooth muscle, T cells, germ cells, Leydig cells, macrophage, and Sertoli cells, which was similar to the scRNA-seq results.
source: A total of 41,708 high-quality cells were obtained from scATAC-seq analysis (Supplementary file 2), and they were also annotated with B cells, endothelial cells, PMCs, Schwann cell, smooth muscle, T cells, germ cells, Leydig cells, macrophage, and Sertoli cells, which was similar to the scRNA-seq results (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a comparison between scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Sertoli cells specifically express classical markers AMH and SOX9.
source: For instance, we observed that Sertoli cells, in addition to specifically expressing classical markers AMH and SOX9 (Fröjdman et al., 2000; Lasala et al., 2011), also exhibited strong expression of APOA1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a cited observation from the literature (Fröjdman et al., 2000; Lasala et al., 2011) confirmed in the study's data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Sertoli cells exhibit strong expression of APOA1.
source: For instance, we observed that Sertoli cells, in addition to specifically expressing classical markers AMH and SOX9 (Fröjdman et al., 2000; Lasala et al., 2011), also exhibited strong expression of APOA1 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a novel observation from the study's data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: PMCs express the classical marker MYH11.
source: Furthermore, we identified that the PMCs not only expressed the classical marker MYH11 (Lottrup et al., 2014), which is concurrently highly expressed in smooth muscle cells, displaying limited specificity, but also demonstrated higher specificity in the expression of DPEP1, suggesting its potential as a specific marker for PMCs.
evidence: This is a cited observation from the literature (Lottrup et al., 2014) confirmed in the study.

claim: DPEP1 demonstrates higher specificity as a marker for PMCs compared to MYH11.
source: Furthermore, we identified that the PMCs not only expressed the classical marker MYH11 (Lottrup et al., 2014), which is concurrently highly expressed in smooth muscle cells, displaying limited specificity, but also demonstrated higher specificity in the expression of DPEP1, suggesting its potential as a specific marker for PMCs.
evidence: This is a novel finding from the study suggesting DPEP1 as a more specific marker for PMCs.

claim: For most cell populations, shifts in chromatin accessibility were aligned with coordinated alterations in gene expression levels.
source: Integrating scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq analysis revealed substantial overlap between the cells profiled in the scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data, implying that for most cell populations shifts in chromatin accessibility were aligned with coordinated alterations in gene expression levels (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the integrated analysis of scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: SSC0/1 and SSC2 are quiescent stem cells and rapidly cycling cells, respectively.
source: As shown in Figure 3A and B, SSC0/1 and SSC2 are quiescent stem cells and rapidly cycling cells, respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the cell cycle analysis shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Maintenance of SSC pluripotency is transcriptionally governed by the downregulation of ID4.
source: Maintenance of SSC pluripotency, whether in the G0/G1 phase and G2/M arrest SSC0/SSC1, or rapid cycling SSC2, is transcriptionally governed by the downregulation of ID4 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the transcriptional dynamics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The pivotal driving genes promoting the transition of SSC2 into differentiating Diffing SPG cells and progressing through mitosis are upregulated DMRT1 and PABPC4.
source: The pivotal driving genes promoting the transition of SSC2 into differentiating Diffing SPG cells and progressing through mitosis are upregulated DMRT1 and PABPC4 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the transcriptional dynamics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: BEND2 takes the central regulatory position as germ cell development proceeds into meiosis.
source: As BEND2 takes the central regulatory position, germ cell development officially proceeds into meiosis, marking the transitioned cells (Diffed SPG) in a mixed transitional state concurrently undergoing both mitosis and meiosis (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the transcriptional dynamics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The molecular markers distinguishing between the PreLep and SPT3 subpopulations included C18orf63, MNS1, CCDC42, LDHC, TMIGD3, AC113189.2, and FLJ40194.
source: The molecular markers distinguishing between the PreLep and SPT3 subpopulations included C18orf63, MNS1, CCDC42, LDHC, TMIGD3, AC113189.2, and FLJ40194 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a result from the transcriptional dynamics analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: There were 665 DEGs between the OA and NOA groups in germ cells, including 367 downregulated genes and 298 upregulated genes.
source: The volcano map showed that there were 665 DEGs between the OA and NOA groups, including 367 downregulated genes and 298 upregulated genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A.

claim: DEGs in germ cells between OA and NOA groups were mainly associated with meiotic cell cycle and meiotic cell cycle process.
source: GO analysis showed that DEGs were mainly associated with meiotic cell cycle and meiotic cell cycle process (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4C.

claim: DEGs in germ cells between OA and NOA groups were primarily involved in cell cycle and DNA replication.
source: KEGG analysis showed that DEGs were primarily involved in cell cycle and DNA replication (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is a result from the KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4D.

claim: CDC6 may play an important role in spermatogenesis.
source: Overall, CDC6 may play an important role in spermatogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of differential peaks and gene expression patterns.

source: As shown in Figure 3E, PIWIL4, C19orf84, and ST3GAL4 were specifically expressed in SSC0 (belong to cluster 2).
evidence: This is a result from the beam analysis shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ID4, TCF3, and UTF1 were specifically expressed in SSC1.
source: ID4, TCF3, and UTF1 were specifically expressed in SSC1 (belong to cluster 2).
evidence: This is a result from the beam analysis.

claim: DMRT1, ASB9, and NANOS3 were the main specifically expressed genes in SSC2.
source: DMRT1, ASB9, and NANOS3 were the main specifically expressed genes in SSC2 (belong to cluster 3).
evidence: This is a result from the beam analysis.

claim: DYNLL1, APRT, and MKI67 were specifically expressed in Diffing-SPG.
source: DYNLL1, APRT, and MKI67 were specifically expressed in Diffing-SPG (belong to cluster 1/2/3).
evidence: This is a result from the beam analysis.

claim: CTCFL, TEX19, and SMC1B were specifically expressed in Diffed-SPG.
source: CTCFL, TEX19, and SMC1B were specifically expressed in Diffed-SPG (belong to cluster 1).

claim: The transcription of SSC1 and SSC2 was very active during reproductive development.
source: Heatmaps of transcription factors showed that the transcription of SSC1 and SSC2 was very active during reproductive development (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an observation from the transcription factor heatmap analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: SPT2/3 was almost transcribed in silence.
source: In contrast, SPT2/3 was almost transcribed in silence.
evidence: This is an observation from the transcription factor heatmap analysis.

claim: No cluster-specific distinctive features were identified in SC1 as the marker genes (TF, SLC16A1, and CCNL1) of SC1 were also highly expressed in other Sertoli cell subclusters.
source: Of note, no cluster-specific distinctive features were identified in SC1 as the marker genes (TF, SLC16A1, and CCNL1) of SC1 were also highly expressed in other Sertoli cell subclusters (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from the marker gene expression analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: SOX2, NF1B, and COL27A1 were preferentially expressed in SC2.
source: SOX2, NF1B, and COL27A1 were preferentially expressed in SC2.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

source: SPATS1, LINC01120, and LINC01206 were specifically expressed in SC3.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

claim: BEND2, PRAP1, and TEX1 were specifically expressed in SC4.
source: BEND2, PRAP1, and TEX1 were specifically expressed in SC4.

claim: PLPP2, BEND4, and RHOXF1 were specifically expressed in SC5.
source: PLPP2, BEND4, and RHOXF1 were specifically expressed in SC5.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

claim: MLC1, SMCP, and NUPR2 were highly expressed in SC6.
source: MLC1, SMCP, and NUPR2 were highly expressed in SC6.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

claim: FLRT2, CFH, and BST2 were specifically expressed in SC7.
source: FLRT2, CFH, and BST2 were specifically expressed in SC7.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

claim: TMIGD3, PGAM2, and CCDC62 were specifically expressed in SC8.
source: TMIGD3, PGAM2, and CCDC62 were specifically expressed in SC8.
evidence: This is a result from the marker gene expression analysis.

claim: There were 414 DEGs in Sertoli cells between the NOA and OA groups, comprising 291 downregulated and 123 upregulated genes in the OA group.
source: The volcano plot revealed a total of 414 DEGs, comprising 291 downregulated and 123 upregulated genes in the OA group (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the differential expression analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: DEGs in Sertoli cells between OA and NOA groups were predominantly associated with meiotic cell cycle, meiotic cell cycle process, and germ cell development.
source: GO analysis indicated that these DEGs were predominantly associated with meiotic cell cycle, meiotic cell cycle process, and germ cell development, as depicted in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.
evidence: This is a result from the GO enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: DEGs in Sertoli cells between OA and NOA groups were primarily involved in cell cycle, cytokine−cytokine receptor interaction, and TNF signaling pathway.
source: Additionally, KEGG analysis revealed that the DEGs were primarily involved in cell cycle, cytokine−cytokine receptor interaction, and TNF signaling pathway, as shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.
evidence: This is a result from the KEGG pathway enrichment analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: The trajectory of Sertoli cell development was determined to initiate with state 3 as beginning and reached a terminally differentiate state of state 2 and state 1.
source: The trajectory was determined to initiate with state 3 as beginning and reached a terminally differentiate state of state 2 and state 1 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a result from the pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: State 1 mainly included SC3/4/5 clusters, state 2 mainly included SC2/6/8 clusters, and state 3 mainly included SC1/7 clusters.
source: According to Figure 5B, state 1 mainly included SC3/4/5 clusters, state 2 mainly included SC2/6/8 clusters, and state 3 mainly included SC1/7 clusters.
evidence: This is a result from the pseudotime trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: State 1 expressed markers EGR3, CTSL, PCNA, MK167, and KRT18 associated with immature Sertoli cells.
source: However, in this study, we identified three distinct states of Sertoli cells, with state 1 expressing markers EGR3, CTSL, PCNA, MK167, and KRT18 associated with immature Sertoli cells (Zhao et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a result from the study with cited support from the literature (Zhao et al., 2020).

claim: State 3 expressed markers TF, HOPX, and DEF119 indicative of mature Sertoli cells.
source: while state 3 expressed markers, such as TF, HOPX, and DEF119, indicative of mature Sertoli cells (Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a result from the study with cited support from the literature (Zhao et al., 2020).

claim: State 2 is defined as a further maturation Sertoli cells, falling between immature and mature states.
source: State 2, falling between immature and mature states, does not belong to either category. Therefore, it is defined as a further maturation Sertoli cells, aligning with previously reported findings in the literature (Guo et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a novel classification proposed by the authors with cited support from the literature (Guo et al., 2021; Zhao et al., 2020).

claim: The differentiation process of Sertoli cells is SC3, SC4, SC5, SC2, SC6, SC8, SC1, and SC7.
source: According to the latent time of RNA rate, the differentiation process is SC3, SC4, SC5, SC2, SC6, SC8, SC1, and SC7 (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a result from the RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SC4 (PRAP1) is defined as immature Sertoli cells.
source: Based on the above result, we identified three novel Sertoli cell subtypes (namely SC4/7/8) and their specific markers, and defined SC4 (PRAP1) as immature, SC7 (BST2) as mature, and SC8 (CCDC62) as further mature (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a novel classification proposed by the authors based on their analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SC7 (BST2) is defined as mature Sertoli cells.
source: Based on the above result, we identified three novel Sertoli cell subtypes (namely SC4/7/8) and their specific markers, and defined SC4 (PRAP1) as immature, SC7 (BST2) as mature, and SC8 (CCDC62) as further mature (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a novel classification proposed by the authors based on their analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: SC8 (CCDC62) is defined as further mature Sertoli cells.
source: Based on the above result, we identified three novel Sertoli cell subtypes (namely SC4/7/8) and their specific markers, and defined SC4 (PRAP1) as immature, SC7 (BST2) as mature, and SC8 (CCDC62) as further mature (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a novel classification proposed by the authors based on their analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Sertoli cells in state 1 were mainly involved in cell cycle, meiotic cell cycle, and spermatogenesis.
source: Sertoli cells in state 1 were mainly involved in cell cycle, meiotic cell cycle, and spermatogenesis.
evidence: This is a result from the GO analysis of Sertoli cells in different states.

claim: Sertoli cells in state 2 were mainly involved in platelet degranulation, lipid metabolic process, and steroid biosynthetic process.
source: Sertoli cells in state 2 were mainly involved in platelet degranulation, lipid metabolic process, and steroid biosynthetic process.
evidence: This is a result from the GO analysis of Sertoli cells in different states.

claim: Sertoli cells in state 3 were mainly involved in extracellular matrix organization, SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane and viral transcription.
source: Sertoli cells in state 3 were mainly involved in extracellular matrix organization, SRP-dependent cotranslational protein targeting to membrane and viral transcription.
